name: approach to neonatal care overview
title: The newborn needing extra care, sorted by what it must be kept: pink (resuscitation at birth, then respiratory distress told apart by who, timing and chest x-ray), warm (hypothermia), sweet (hypoglycemia screening and treatment), free of sepsis (risk, workup, antibiotics) and the yellow baby (jaundice red flags, investigations, phototherapy); each column gives presentation, numbered assessment and treatment, with a panel on routine care before discharge

nodes.title: A newborn: keep it PINK, WARM and SWEET, and think SEPSIS in any sick baby
lines: normal: heart rate 120–160 · respiratory rate 40–60 · blood pressure 55–65/35–40 · axillary temperature 36.5–36.8 °C · never ignore tachypnea or tachycardia
1 in 10 need some help at birth · < 1% need extensive resuscitation · 3% have a major malformation

nodes.title: Resuscitation at birth
lines: the goal: ventilation

nodes.title: Respiratory distress
lines: work of breathing: grunting

nodes.title: Hypothermia
lines: CANNOT shiver

nodes.title: Hypoglycemia
lines: glycogen lasts 8–10 h · gluconeogenesis normal only by day 2–4
fat: 16% of body weight at 40 weeks, 1% at 27

nodes.title: Neonatal sepsis
lines: the commonest life-threatening newborn problem · 1–10 per 1000, 1 in 250 preterm
early < 3 days, late > 3 days

nodes.title: Jaundice
lines: most: exaggerated physiologic or breastfeeding jaundice

nodes.title: Term? good tone? breathing or crying?
lines: • YES → skin to skin, routine care
• NO → warm, dry, position, stimulate, clear the airway

nodes.title: Who, and when?
lines: • term, cesarean with no labour, diabetic mother: at birth, gets better
• preterm, diabetic mother: at birth, worse to day 3–4
• stressed baby: from birth

nodes.title: Cold stress
lines: • wet, naked, large surface area
• little fat, few reserves

nodes.title: Jittery, irritable, lethargic, poor feeding
lines: can be a sign of SEPSIS

nodes.title: Screen if at risk
lines: • small (< 10th) or large (> 90th centile)
• infant of a diabetic mother
• preterm < 37 weeks, maternal labetalol
• late preterm given steroids · asphyxia · metabolic, Beckwith-Wiedemann
• too little store: IUGR, maternal hypertension, twins · too much use: cold, sepsis

nodes.title: Subtle
lines: • temperature < 36.3 or > 37.2 °C
• apnea, grunting, fast or slow heart
• capillary refill > 3 s, mottled, grey
• poor feeding, distension, bloody stool, glucose < 2.6
• floppy or jittery, seizure

nodes.title: Risk
lines: • chorioamnionitis ×4 · maternal GBS, past GBS baby, GBS in urine
• membranes ruptured > 18 h ×10 (to 1%) · preterm
• fetal tachycardia · meconium ×2
• 5-minute Apgar < 6 ×36

nodes.title: Head to toe: blanch the nose
lines: colour does NOT predict the level

nodes.title: RED FLAGS
lines: • jaundice in the first 24 h, or > 2 weeks (term)
• cord bilirubin > 68 · rise > 85 μmol/L/day, or total > 340
• direct > 30, or > 20% of total · unwell baby

nodes.title: 1 · Apnea, gasping or heart rate < 100
lines: → VENTILATE within the first minute + pulse oximeter

nodes.title: 2 · Laboured or persistently cyanotic
lines: → pulse oximeter, oxygen if needed, consider continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP)

nodes.title: Chest x-ray
lines: • fluid in the fissures, sunburst streaks, normal or high volume: transient tachypnea of the newborn (fluid not reabsorbed)
• ground glass, low volume, air bronchograms: respiratory distress syndrome (no surfactant)

nodes.title: Patchy or black rim
lines: • patchy: meconium aspiration (air trapping, PPHN, surfactant inactivated) or pneumonia (posterior triangle)
• black rim: pneumothorax, spontaneous or positive pressure

nodes.title: Uses up glucose
lines: → check SWEET

nodes.title: 1 · Glucose 2 h after the first feed
2 · Goal ≥ 2.6 mmol/L
lines: ≥ 3.3 after 72 h · at goal: no more sticks

nodes.title: UNWELL or PRETERM → full workup
lines: • also ANY fever, seizure, unexplained apnea, instability, lethargy
• blood, urine, cerebrospinal fluid cultures
• blood count (white cells ↑ or ↓), C-reactive protein, clotting
• chest x-ray if breathing · herpes simplex virus (HSV) swabs

nodes.title: WELL + risk factors
lines: observe 24 h before discharge

nodes.title: 1 · Bilirubin on EVERY baby at 24 h
lines: skin meter or blood · plot on the curve
causes: sepsis, ABO or Rh isoimmunization, membrane or enzyme defects (G6PD), cephalohematoma, polycythemia, ceftriaxone or sulfa drugs, breast milk

nodes.title: 2 · Red flag → work up
lines: • total + direct bilirubin, hemoglobin
• direct antiglobulin test (DAT)
• mother's and baby's blood groups

nodes.title: Targets
lines: • chest rise, breath sounds
• heart rate > 100
• oxygen saturation only 85–95% by 10 min: transient hypoxia is normal

nodes.title: Pneumonia: any time, septic risk factors
lines: group B Streptococcus, gram negatives → see SICK

nodes.title: 2 · < 1500 g → incubator
lines: radiant warmer, humidity

nodes.title: 1 · SYMPTOMATIC = emergency
lines: intravenous (IV) dextrose bolus + infusion: it injures neurons

nodes.title: 2 · Well: early, frequent feeds
lines: then IV dextrose, glucagon

nodes.title: 1 · Antibiotics ASAP: never wait and see
lines: • ampicillin + gentamicin
• + acyclovir for HSV
• GBS, E. coli, Klebsiella, Listeria, HSV · in hospital: coagulase-negative staph, Candida
• mortality 2–4% · early E. coli in term infants 6–10%

nodes.title: 2 · Support
lines: ventilation, circulation, disseminated intravascular coagulation

nodes.title: 1 · Phototherapy + treat the cause
lines: • light turns bilirubin into a soluble isomer (lumirubin)
• start lower if < 38 weeks, albumin < 30, hemolysis, sepsis, unstable

nodes.title: 2 · Not enough → IV immunoglobulin or exchange transfusion
lines: • untreated: lethargy, floppy, poor suck → stiff, arched (opisthotonos), high-pitched cry, fever → seizures, coma
• kernicterus: stained, dead basal ganglia + brainstem neurons

panels.title: Every newborn before going home
items: Apgar at 1 and 5 min, 0–2 each: appearance, pulse (< 100 scores 1), grimace, activity (tone), respiration
full exam within 24 h: dysmorphic features, heart (may have no murmur), a patent gut · urine and meconium passed
vitamin K intramuscular (prevents early and classic bleeding; oral is less effective) + erythromycin eye ointment (gonococcal ophthalmia) at birth

screens: pulse oximetry right hand vs a foot at 24–36 h (specificity 99.9%, sensitivity 76.5%; false + pulmonary hypertension, pneumonia; misses coarctation with open duct) · Ontario newborn screen · hearing (6 in 1000: otoacoustic emissions, then AABR)
weight: loses up to 10%, back to birth weight by 7–10 days, then 25 g/day · doubles by 5 months, triples by 1 year · seen 72 h after discharge · vaccines from 2 months

panels.title: Transition at birth + definitions
items: fetus: lungs get 4% of cardiac output, saturation ~60%, right-to-left via foramen ovale + ductus
first breaths: pulmonary resistance ↓ · cord clamped, systemic pressure ↑ · lungs get 100% · ductus + foramen close
surfactant: type 2 pneumocytes · 90% phospholipid · DPPC (lecithin) lowers surface tension
term 37–40 · late preterm 34–36+6 · moderate 32–34 · very < 32 · extremely ≤ 25 weeks

panels.title: Feeding, sleep, vitamin K
items: 115–120 kcal/kg/day · milk and formula 20 kcal/oz · 30–60 mL every 2–3 h
breast milk alone for 6 months, continue at least 1 year · vitamin D for ALL breastfed · iron-rich solids
safe sleep: on the BACK, firm flat crib in the parents' room, no bedding, no co-bedding, no smoke
vitamin K deficiency: early < 24 h (maternal antiepileptics) · classic 2–7 days · late 2–12 weeks (malabsorption)
